title: From here to there: How Torontonians get everywhere
description: Toronto is filled with pathways, not only paved roads, but paths, rivers, and trails. Over the long history of Toronto these pathways have been covered up or forgotten. Today we will help you rediscover these paths and show how they form the Toronto we know today.

stops_data.title: The Great Fill
stops_data.description: St Clair, one of the oldest streets in Toronto, was not always the street it is today.

stops_data.title: The Russell Hill Emergency Exit - The Disaster That Shaped The TTC
stops_data.description: A plethora of problems that led to one of the worst subway disasters in North America, the Russell Hill Emergency Exit tells an extensive and profound story of the disaster that shaped the TTC.
stops_data.text: The Toronto Transit Commission is used by around 2.5 million Torontonians daily. It’s an instrumental part of our daily lifestyle systems here in Toronto, allowing us to get from place to place via a quick subway, bus, or streetcar ride. But what we now know as the safe and reliable TTC that we all use and trust was once built on an illusion of safety, a system sustained more by its reputation than by its reality. In this audio file, you’ll learn more about North America’s worst subway accident, the Russell Hill Disaster that killed 3 people and the emergency exit passengers used to escape the catastrophe.

stops_data.title: The Protests That Changed Toronto
stops_data.description: In the 50’s, the city dreamed of a highway that would connect downtown and the northern suburbs. However when it began, the people of the neighbourhoods it would cut through, like the Annex and Rathnelly, rose up and fought back, eventually stopping it before it could cut through their communities.
stops_data.text: The Spadina Bridge and Nordheimer Ravine serve as powerful reminders of how close Toronto came to losing one of its most beautiful natural spaces. This stop will explore the history of the proposed Spadina Expressway, a controversial project from the 1950s that would have cut through the ravine to connect downtown to the suburbs. As we stand here, we’ll imagine how this quiet green space could have become a busy highway, look at early fire maps showing planned development across the ravine, and reflect on how community protests — including those by nearby residents in the Republic of Rathnelly were able to help stop the project and preserve the area we see today.

stops_data.title: Transportation as a natural design
stops_data.description: For millennia things have been moving all throughout the very land that you are standing on right now. This necessity to shift, to move from one place to another, to deliver, to transport, runs deep into the intrinsic design of all natural things. It is only due to us humans, the ones who believe that we are the only movers within the world, that these natural transportation systems have become hidden. This stop aims to uncover them and allow us all to learn the patterns of the past.
stops_data.text: This stop on the walking tour will take you through the history of the very land that you are standing on reading this. You will be brought through many of the hidden modes of transportation that surround you but remain unseen. Specifically, the stop begins by going through the history and importance of the once surface level Castle Frank Brook: what it used to be and why it is the way it is now. Then, you will learn more about the importance of the Nordheimer ravine’s ecosystem to historical modes of transportation. After that the stop goes into detail on the benefits of and how to identify Ontario’s provincial tree, the Eastern White Pine. Finally, the tour ends by going into detail on some of the most inspiring transporters on the planet, the Yellow Bellied Sapsucker.

stops_data.title: The Road That Transports Time
stops_data.description: Poplar Plains may seem like a small insignificant road but that could not be further from the truth, this road has a history so rich, it tells the story of Toronto’s transportation throughout time.
stops_data.text: Poplar Plains may be a small road but it displays the evolution of variety of transportation in Toronto. This stop will start on Poplar Plains Road at the entrance to the Nordheimer Ravine. While making our way South to Dupont, we will explore the history of the bike path on Poplar Plains Road and it’s significance to the city of Toronto. After discussing the bike path, we will go back in time and explore the historical usage of Poplar Plains road by the Anishnaabe and Northwest Company. We will end of this stop at the foot of Poplar Plains road by the intersection of Dupont and explore the evolution and significance of this railway.
